instruction:
The apps for this task are already open in separate browser tabs and logged in (Stripe, Google Sheets, and Gmail). Just switch between these tabs to do the task -- no sign-in or URL needed.

First, read the churn-confirmation email in Gmail: it names the customer whose subscription has churned and must be canceled before you pull the report. Find that customer's subscription in Stripe and cancel it -- open the subscription's detail page, click Cancel, and choose 'Cancel immediately' so its status becomes 'canceled'. A canceled subscription must NOT appear in the MRR report.

Then build a subscription MRR (monthly recurring revenue) report from Stripe into the 'MRR' tab of the Google Sheet. Consider only subscriptions whose status is 'active' or 'past_due' (skip canceled/trialing/paused -- including the one you just canceled). For each, compute its monthly amount in dollars: sum over its items of unit_amount(cents)/100 * quantity, then normalize to monthly -- if the price interval is 'year' divide by 12, if 'month' keep as is (round each subscription's MRR to cents). Fill columns Customer, Status, Interval, MRR -- one row per qualifying subscription, sorted by MRR descending. The Interval column must contain literally 'month' or 'year' (lowercase), matching the price's billing interval. Below the rows add: a 'Total MRR' row (col A label, col D = sum of all MRR), and an 'At Risk MRR' row (col A label, col D = sum of MRR for past_due subscriptions only). All money displayed with two decimals.
